correctness.rationale: Verified the exact survival map Φ(s)=(exp(s^(1−s))−1)/(e−1) by algebraic subtraction of the source CDF. Expansion s^(1−s)=s−s²log s+O(s³log²s), then exp(t) gives s−s²log s+s²/2+O(s³log²s). The normalized hazard ratio equals (1−s−s log s)t exp(t)/(exp(t)−1), tending to 1 under the positive-density condition. Two-sided constant tail bounds imply equivalence of every positive nonnegative moment threshold; regular variation and Pareto quantile scaling follow by tail inversion. Independent numeric checks at s=0.1, 0.01, 10^−4, 10^−6 confirm limits and controlled residual order; these samples do not prove the endpoint theorem. The limiting scale 1/(e−1) is NOT an all-baseline equality at finite x.
